propositions: GitHub code-scanning alert #88 flags bare substring containment in upstream-URL assertion that accepts lookalike hosts prefixed or suffixed with attacker-controlled domains.
The old expression `assert "pandoc.org" in text or "github.com/jgm/pandoc" in text` accepts https://notpandoc.org and https://pandoc.org.evil.com, neither of which actionably points upstream.
Replace substring checks with a scheme+host-anchored negative-lookahead regex that rejects both prefix and suffix lookalikes while accepting valid real NOTICE mentions.
The new regex pattern uses explicit end-of-host boundaries: `(?![\w.-])` after `pandoc\.org` and `(?![\w-])` after the github path to block non-actionable variants.
Test suite confirms the fix: pytest passes on real NOTICE, RED demonstration rejects both lookalike classes, and CodeQL alert #88 clears after merge without dismissal.
